prize_parts.citation: for the analysis of firm heterogeneity and market selection in international trade

statement.case_for: My configuration has changed from the three-recipient B020 proposal to a Melitz-only award. The discussion reinforced that B020 is an exceptionally mature and consequential achievement: the canonical framework made firm productivity heterogeneity and endogenous selection central to trade theory and generated a durable theoretical, empirical, and quantitative programme. But the same discussion made clear that Helpman's and Redding's important connected contributions do not have the same unambiguous relation to the originating model. A Melitz-only award with a citation confined to heterogeneity and selection states a precise, foundational achievement without claiming credit for the entire subsequent literature.
statement.case_against: The narrower allocation sacrifices recognition of major complementary work on the broader heterogeneous-firm trade programme, including work relevant to trade gains and empirical development. It also makes the prize less representative of that programme's collective evolution. B031 remains a highly mature alternative, while B014 offers an unusually important empirical infrastructure; neither, however, improves on B020's combination of a sharply identifiable foundational mechanism and long-run influence.

responses.point: Krusell argues that Melitz is the clear originator of the canonical heterogeneous-firm framework and questions whether Helpman and Redding should be included when the achievement is defined around that core model.
responses.response: I now agree that this distinction should determine the allocation. The three-person formulation was defensible only under a broader programme-level citation, but that breadth created the attribution problem it was intended to solve. Defining the prize around the canonical analysis of firm heterogeneity and selection makes Melitz the exact and sufficient recipient.

responses.point: Dreber Almenberg maintains that Helpman and Redding are defensible co-laureates if B020 is defined as the broader programme of heterogeneity, selection, and trade gains, while warning against claiming credit for the whole literature.
responses.response: I agree that the broader programme has multiple central contributors, which is precisely why I no longer think its full scope can be allocated cleanly through this configuration. The narrower Melitz citation preserves the achievement's scientific core and leaves clear that later theoretical and empirical extensions are not being absorbed into a single-recipient claim.

responses.point: Krusell supports B031 as a mature account of collateral constraints and financial amplification but acknowledges that it joins collateral-cycle and financial-accelerator strands developed across distinct papers and coauthor groups.
responses.response: That qualification remains material in comparison with the revised B020 configuration. B031 identifies powerful and enduring mechanisms, but its proposed trio still requires combining related strands into one shared achievement. The Melitz-only B020 formulation is more exact in linking the citation, foundational contribution, and credited scholar.

uncertainties: Whether a Melitz-only citation should mention gains from trade, given that this may broaden the claim beyond the canonical selection framework.

Whether the committee should instead prefer B031's macro-financial importance or B014's administrative-data measurement contribution despite their respective attribution and interpretation reservations.
statement.conflict_note: The supplied profile records long-running collaboration with Peter J. Klenow, a credited candidate on B036. B036 is not part of my preferred configuration or alternatives; if it is considered, this connection may require recusal. No apparent connection to Marc J. Melitz or to the alternatives' proposed laureates is supplied.
